_what: Experimentally supported aggregation-critical regions. The validation set.
_why: A benchmark of aggregation predictors is only as sound as the ground truth it scores against. Nothing in this project is sounder than this table, so it carries provenance per row rather than per file.

_numbering.TRIOBP-1: 652-residue frame of NP_008963.3 (UniProt Q9H2D6-7). Papers using the older 593-residue frame need 59 ADDED. One paper gives the shorter variant as 593 in one place and 597 in another. A table that mixes frames without normalising is silently wrong by 59 residues.

_columns.construct: WHICH CONSTRUCT established it. A region can be necessary in one construct and dispensable in another; both results can be correct. Without this column the benchmark scores against a moving target.
_columns.found_by: how the region was discovered. 'prediction' rows are CIRCULAR for a predictor benchmark and must be analysed separately.
_columns.verified_against_publisher_pdf: false means nobody has opened the source and checked this row.

regions.CAUTION_2026_11_15: THIS IS A DOCKING RESTRAINT, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Nothing was deposited -- no coordinates, no chemical shifts, no EM map, no accession, and the paper has no data-availability section. The EM was negative-stain TEM at 120 kV with no resolution reported, and the model is a MODELLER protomer built with ANTIPARALLEL BETA-STRAND RESTRAINTS IMPOSED AS INPUT (segments 716-737 and 739-761) then docked into that envelope. Re-modelling it would re-assert the input, not confirm the topology. The paper also states its own boundary two ways, 716-761 and 717-761. The 2025 follow-up states verbatim 'No data was used for the research described in the article'.

regions.evidence: truncation and deletion in cells; no single D, I, S or C region aggregates alone
regions.construct: full-length and domain constructs in SH-SY5Y; insolubility assay in HEK293. NECESSITY AND SUFFICIENCY ARE NOT ON EQUAL FOOTING HERE -- read this column before quoting the paper's abstract. NECESSARY: deleting 384-415 from full-length 1-854, and from 1-836 and 1-655, abolishes aggregation in all three (Fig 5D-F). SUFFICIENT: the Discussion says 384-415 'was both sufficient for aggregation', but 384-415 WAS NEVER EXPRESSED ALONE. What was expressed alone is the whole linker, 384-538 (155 aa, Fig 4D), and 1-415 (Fig 5C). So sufficiency is established for the linker and for 384-415 IN THE CONTEXT OF 1-383 -- not for the 32-mer in isolation.
regions.found_by: experimental truncation and deletion; NOT circular. No aggregation predictor was used to find it. The only prediction mentioned is post-hoc description ('would be predicted to be alpha-helical', citing Soares 2011, a review). It also sits OUTSIDE all four ESPRIT-defined domains -- 'not found within any of 94 most stable DISC1 fragments' -- so the structural screen missed it too. CIRCULARITY RE-CHECKED 16 Nov 2026 AND STILL CLEAN, BUT NARROWLY: Zaharija's 2025 thesis §4.3.5 DOES run five aggregation predictors (TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid, MetAmyl, ANuPP) on full-length DISC1 -- but AFTER the region was mapped by truncation and deletion, as a post-hoc mechanistic check, and the thesis presents the predictions as complementing a finding already in hand. The region was NOT found by prediction. This row stays in the non-circular set. It does, however, mean the legacy-predictor scores for DISC1 are published prior art.
regions.note: ADDED 15 Nov 2026; SOURCE READ 16 Nov 2026. A ~32-residue linker C-terminal of the D region, outside all four structured domains. CONTRADICTS the C-terminal in vitro result above, and both groups acknowledge the conflict. It is also the second case of the central pattern: an inter-domain linker in a coiled-coil scaffold protein, missed by every predictor. Caveat: same lab as the TRIOBP-1 work, so this is a second case rather than independent replication.
regions.sequence_provenance: RETRIEVED FROM UNIPROT 15 Nov 2026, not transcribed by hand. rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9NRI5.fasta, header 'sp|Q9NRI5|DISC1_HUMAN ... PE=1 SV=3', full length 854, which matches the 854 aa shown on the entry page the author checked. Residues 384-415 inclusive, 1-based, 32 residues -- consistent with the '~32-residue linker' in STATE.md. IMPORTANT: UniProt confirms the SEQUENCE for this range, NOT that the range is right. The 384-415 boundaries come from the source paper and remain verified_against_publisher_pdf: false.
regions.GATEKEEPER_RESULT_2026_11_15: 18.8% gatekeeper (2 Pro + 4 charged of 32). THIS BREAKS THE HEADLINE. The worst crystallised steric zipper is 16.7% (tau VQIVYK and SOD1 30-35), so this region is +2.1 points above it -- indistinguishable. 18 of its 27 hexapeptide windows are at or below the worst zipper, minimum 0.0% at ISLHFQ. The reported 'psychiatric regions 48.0% to 50.0% (n=2)' was carried by TRIOBP-1 324-348 at 48.0% plus DISC1 716-761 at 50.0% -- and 716-761 is the docking-restraint row found by a RADAR sequence search, which the found_by column exists to exclude. With the honest DISC1 row the separation does not generalise: ONE region is gatekeeper-rich, the other is not.
regions.verified_against: Zaharija & Bradshaw, bioRxiv 2023.08.03.551216v1 (read in full) PLUS Zaharija B (2025) PhD thesis, University of Rijeka (READ IN FULL 16 Nov 2026, key zaharija2025thesis). RANGE SETTLED AT 384-415: the thesis's Table 11 names the actual plasmids 'DISC1 (delta-384-415)', 'DISC1 (1-655 delta-384-415)' and 'DISC1 (1-836 delta-384-415)', and both §4.3.4 and Conclusion 3.1 give AA 384-415 and 'the 32 AA'. The preprint's delta-384-414 was a typo. One stray slip remains in the thesis itself: Figure 48's caption says 'AA 383-415'.
regions.range_provenance: READ, 16 Nov 2026. Discussion: 'AA 384-415, immediately C-terminal of the D region'. Three internal checks agree: D region ends at 383; 1-383 does not aggregate while 1-415 does (Fig 5B,C); and 383+32=415 matches 'these 32 amino acids were deleted', which matches the 32-residue UniProt string already stored. ONE-RESIDUE SLIP IN THE SOURCE, DOES NOT AFFECT US: the p.9 body text writes the deletion constructs as delta-384-414 three times (31 residues) while Figure 5A and panels D-F label them delta-384-415 and the same sentence says 32. 384-415 is right.
regions.domain_frame_from_source: ESPRIT regions, Yerabham 2017 via this paper's Fig 1/Results: D 257-383, I 539-655, S 635-738, C 691-836. I/S overlap at 635-655 and S/C at 691-738. Second slip: Results prints 'AA 539-738' for BOTH I+S and S+C; S+C is 635-836 per Fig 3A and the Discussion.
regions.circularity_basis: Found by truncation and deletion in cells. Re-checked 16 Nov 2026 against Zaharija's 2025 thesis, which DOES run five aggregation predictors on DISC1 -- but only AFTER the region was mapped, as a post-hoc mechanistic check. Prediction after mapping does not contaminate.
regions.stratum_basis: RESOLVED 16 Nov 2026 FROM THE LITERATURE, NO RUN OF OURS REQUIRED, and it resolves cleanly because the registered legacy arm is narrower than the thesis's tool list. Zaharija 2025 section 4.3.5 ran five predictors on full-length DISC1 and FOUR OF FIVE gave "aggregation/amyloid formation hotspots dispersed throughout the entirety of the protein sequence" -- they did NOT single out the linker. Those four include every tool in PREREGISTRATION 5.1: TANGO (2004), AGGRESCAN (2007) and FoldAmyloid (2010). AGAINST THE REGISTERED LEGACY ARM THIS ROW IS UNAMBIGUOUSLY DISCORDANT.
regions.THE_ANUPP_EXCEPTION_AND_WHY_IT_IS_NOT_A_: ONE OF THE FIVE DID FIND IT. ANuPP (2021) named AA 387-395 and AA 400-415 as having the highest nucleation capacity. VERIFIED 16 Nov 2026: both lie entirely inside 384-415, so this is a precise hit and not a vague overlap. ANuPP is NOT in the frozen legacy arm (PREREGISTRATION 5.1 = TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid, ProA), so it does not muddy this row's stratum. BUT IT IS IMPORTANT FOR A DIFFERENT REASON -- see _ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1 at the top level of this file. It must be cited, not rediscovered.
regions.frame_verified: CLOSED 16 Nov 2026, a task that had been outstanding since the thesis was read. The thesis input was full-length human L-variant DISC1 as RefSeq NP_061132.2, NOT UniProt Q9NRI5, and the register flagged "VERIFY THE FRAMES MATCH". THEY ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL: both 854 aa, sequences equal on direct comparison. So the thesis's residue numbers transfer to our frame with no offset, and CLAUDE.md's DISC1 numbering trap does not bite here.

regions.frame: tau441 / ht40 (2N4R), UniProt P10636-8, 441 aa. The paper fixes this itself: 'The numbering of the amino acids is that of the isoform ht40 containing 441 residues'.
regions.evidence: PHF6. Minimal interaction motif from an unbiased overlapping-peptide scan, with necessity shown by mutagenesis in an isolated construct AND in the full-length protein.
regions.construct: DISCOVERY: membrane-immobilised library of 15-mer peptides at a 3-residue step spanning 253-354 (30 peptides), probed with iodinated PHF43 = [N265-E338 dR2]. NECESSITY: proline-scanning in PHF47; K19dVQI, K19NAE, K19Y310E; and dVQI / NAE in FULL-LENGTH ht23, where both cause 'a complete loss of PHF formation'. THE CONSTRUCT COLUMN MATTERS HERE: the motif was mapped in a dR2 construct and confirmed in intact protein, which is stronger than either alone.
regions.found_by: UNBIASED PEPTIDE-ARRAY SCAN, 2000 -- four years before TANGO. No predictor in the discovery path. Prediction appears only POST HOC.
regions.note: THE CONTROL ARM FOR H4 (PREREGISTRATION.md 9.1). This is the case with the SAME compositional architecture as TRIOBP-1 324-348 -- globally gatekeeper-rich protein, locally zipper-grade hexapeptide -- WHERE THE PREDICTORS SUCCEED. Without it H4 has no positive control and is withdrawn. TWO THINGS TO CARRY INTO ANY WRITE-UP: (1) ROLE CONFLICT -- VQIVYK is also hardcoded as deposited-crystal comparator 2ON9 in scripts/gatekeeper_density.py; it may serve in ONE role per table and the role must be stated. (2) The radiolabel sits INSIDE the motif: Methods say PHF43 was 'iodinated at Tyr-310', and Tyr-310 is the fifth residue of 306VQIVYK311. The mutational work is label-independent and confirms the result, but raise this rather than be shown it.
regions.sequence_provenance: VERIFIED against UniProt P10636-8: residues 306-311 are VQIVYK, exact. The repeat boundaries corroborate it -- PHF6 is the first six residues of R3 (V306-Q336).
regions.verified_against: von Bergen et al. 2000, PNAS 97:5129 -- PUBLISHER PDF READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026, supplied by the author; Figures 1 and 4 additionally inspected as images from PMC25793.
regions.range_provenance: READ. Abstract and Results (iii): 'a minimal hexapeptide interaction motif of 306VQIVYK311 at the beginning of the third internal repeat'. Figure 4 prints the peptide grid, 15-mers at a 3-residue step, so 306-311 is a measurement at 3-residue resolution and not an inference from a coarse grid.
regions.circularity_basis: Unbiased scan; the probe PHF43 came from GluC limited proteolysis, not from a prediction. Prediction is present in the paper but ONLY POST HOC -- Discussion (v) cites Street & Mayo 1999 for beta-propensity. That is the permitted direction. NOTE FOR HONESTY: an audit subagent reported 'no algorithm named anywhere in the paper'; that is FALSE, and we state the post-hoc position ourselves rather than let a reviewer find it.
regions.stratum_basis: DOCUMENTED, not predicted by us. Discussion (v): PHF6 and PHF6* 'are the only two spots in the tau sequence where a beta conformation is strongly predicted'. The predictors FIND this region, which is exactly why it serves as the positive control and NOT as a test of H1/H4.

regions.evidence: PHF6*. A SECOND, independent maximum of interaction in the same peptide scan, centred on Ile-278.
regions.construct: Same membrane scan and same PHF43 probe as 306-311. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY, IT IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW: R2 is DELETED from the PHF43 probe, so the signal cannot come from the probe's own copy of the motif -- which makes the detection cleaner, not weaker. ISOFORM-DEPENDENT: R2 is encoded by exon 10, so PHF6* exists only in 4R isoforms.
regions.found_by: Same unbiased peptide-array scan. Its own binding maximum, not an analogy to PHF6.
regions.note: WEAKER THAN PHF6 AND THE ROW MUST SAY SO: NECESSITY WAS NEVER TESTED FOR PHF6*. Every mutational experiment in the paper targets 306-311 -- the proline scan, K19dVQI, K19NAE, K19Y310E, dVQI/NAE in ht23. PHF6* has a binding maximum and nothing else. It is therefore NOT a second control arm: it is detected inside the SAME single experiment and carries no mutational validation, so the H4 control arm remains n = 1. Independent support would have to come from von Bergen 2001 (JBC 276:48165), where DeltaK280 -- inside PHF6* -- is characterised.
regions.sequence_provenance: VERIFIED against UniProt P10636-8: residues 275-280 are VQIINK, exact. Corroborated by the repeat boundaries -- PHF6* is the first six residues of R2 (V275-S305).
regions.verified_against: von Bergen et al. 2000, PNAS 97:5129 -- PUBLISHER PDF READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026.
regions.range_provenance: READ. Results (iii): 'A second maximum of interaction was centered around Ile-278, covering the sequence 275VQIINK280 (PHF6*).' Figure 4 caption: 'Another cluster of strong interaction occurs around the spots that harbor the analogous sequence in R2.' Verified: Ile-278 lies inside 275-280.
regions.circularity_basis: Same clean scan as PHF6. CORRECTION RECORDED: this row was briefly demoted on 16 Nov on the reasoning that PHF6* sits in R2 and R2 is deleted from the probe, so it must have been named by analogy. That was WRONG -- it confused the probe with the membrane. The membrane spans 253-354 and contains R2; the probe need not.
regions.stratum_basis: Same documented sentence as PHF6: 'the only two spots in the tau sequence where a beta conformation is strongly predicted'.

regions.evidence: NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT for filament assembly, by four independent lines. Necessity: D71-82 does not assemble by sedimentation or EM even after SIX WEEKS, with no random-coil-to-beta transition by CD. Sufficiency: the synthetic 12-mer self-assembles into filaments and seeds full-length alpha-synuclein.
regions.construct: Full-length human alpha-synuclein with an internal deletion and with A76R / A76E substitutions; human beta-synuclein as a NATURAL comparator; an isolated synthetic 12-mer. All in pRK172 / E. coli BL21(DE3), assembled in 100 mM sodium acetate pH 7.0 at 37 C with shaking. CONTROL THAT ISOLATES THE REGION: the a/b-syn hybrid (a-syn 1-97 + b-syn 87-134) assembles at wild-type rate, so the divergent C-terminus is NOT responsible for beta-synuclein's failure.
regions.found_by: COMPARATIVE SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT AGAINST A PARALOGUE THAT NATURALLY LACKS THE REGION. No predictor and no propensity analysis anywhere in the paper; in 2001 none of the tools under test existed.
regions.source: Giasson et al. 2001, J Biol Chem 276(4):2380-2386
regions.note: ENTERS AS A LABELLED TRUE POSITIVE, NOT AS A TEST. 71-82 overlaps ZipperDB-selected NACore 68-78 by eight residues, so this is a region the predictors DO find. ALSO: at 8.3% proline-plus-charge it sits BELOW the worst deposited zipper (16.7%), so it does not support the gatekeeper inversion -- it dilutes it. AND IT TESTS THE GATEKEEPER PREMISE DIRECTLY: A76R and A76E put a single charge into the middle of the hydrophobic core and NEITHER abolished assembly; the paper concludes a single charged residue 'is not sufficient to disrupt the hydrophobic intermolecular interactions driving filament formation'. Cite that rather than rediscover it.
regions.sequence_provenance: VERIFIED against UniProt P37840: residues 71-82 are VTGVTAVAQKTV, exact match to the string printed in the title, abstract, Results and Discussion. CAUTION: the METHODS print the synthetic peptide as 'VTGVTAVAQKTA', ending in Ala. P37840 position 82 is Val, so the Methods string is wrong at the last residue -- almost certainly a typo, since every other mention is correct, but it is the described sequence of the peptide carrying the whole SUFFICIENCY claim (Figs 4E, 4F, 7). Recorded, not silently assumed.
regions.verified_against: Giasson et al. 2001, JBC 276:2380 -- PUBLISHER PDF READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026, supplied by the author.
regions.range_provenance: READ. Abstract: 'a 12-amino acid stretch ((71)VTGVTAVAQKTV(82)) in the middle of the hydrophobic domain'. BOUNDARY EVIDENCE IS SINGLE-SOURCE: the 71/82 boundaries come from the beta-synuclein alignment alone. The protease-resistant fragments F1-F3 map to 61-95 and merely CONTAIN 71-82, so proteolysis corroborates at 35-residue resolution, not at 12.
regions.circularity_basis: Discovery path is a natural deletion in a close paralogue plus limited proteolysis. No algorithm, and none of the relevant tools existed in 2001.
regions.stratum_basis: DOCUMENTED by overlap: 71-82 shares eight residues with NACore 68-78, which was selected by ZipperDB. A region a predictor picked is one the predictors find.

regions.evidence: The structurally ordered core of FUS-LC fibrils, determined by 3D solid-state NMR. 'We therefore conclude that residues 39-95 constitute the structurally ordered core of FUS-LC fibrils', with 55-62 only partially dynamic. Abstract: 'a segment of only 57 residues forms the fibril core, while other segments remain dynamically disordered.' VERIFIED: 39-95 is exactly 57 residues.
regions.construct: FUS low-complexity domain, residues 2-214 ('without the His tag, contains 214 residues'), with an additional N-terminal His tag on the NMR samples. THE CONSTRUCT MATTERS: the core is 57 of 214 residues, so the surrounding 157 residues were present and remained dynamically disordered -- this is a core mapped IN CONTEXT, not an isolated peptide that happened to aggregate.
regions.found_by: STRUCTURE DETERMINATION (solid-state NMR, MCASSIGN assignment). No predictor in the discovery path. Prediction appears ONLY afterwards, and only to record that it failed.
regions.note: THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW ADDED ON 16 Nov 2026, AND IT COMES FROM THE PAPER THAT PRE-EMPTED OUR COMPOSITIONAL CLAIM. Murray 2017 publishes both halves of this project's old shape for FUS -- named predictors failing on a mapped core, and composition failing to discriminate. That cost us the compositional headline (PREREGISTRATION.md 9.1). IT ALSO HANDS BACK THE BEST TEST ROW IN THE SET. See _WHY_THIS_ROW_IS_THE_CONTROL_PAIR_FOR_H4 below.
regions.provenance_note: READ BY THE MAIN SESSION via PMC5650524 (open access), twice, on 16 Nov 2026: once for the predictor passage and once for the core definition. Both quoted verbatim above. The PDF itself has not been opened, so verified_against_publisher_pdf stays FALSE pending that; the SEQUENCE and the 57-residue arithmetic are independently verified against UniProt.
regions.sequence_provenance: RETRIEVED FROM UniProt P35637, residues 39-95, 16 Nov 2026. Length 57, matching the paper's own 'a segment of only 57 residues' -- an independent arithmetic check on the range.
regions.verified_against: Murray et al. 2017, Cell 171:615 -- PMC5650524 full text read by the main session; publisher PDF not yet opened.
regions.range_provenance: READ. 'We therefore conclude that residues 39-95 constitute the structurally ordered core of FUS-LC fibrils.' Corroborated by the abstract's independent residue count (57).
regions.circularity_basis: The core was determined structurally and the predictors were run afterwards, which is the permitted direction. The paper states the direction itself: the core 'is not predicted by computational methods that assess propensities for amyloid formation'.
regions.stratum_basis: DOCUMENTED IN PRINT, WITH THE PREDICTORS NAMED, which is the strongest form of assignment available and requires no run of our own. Discussion, 'What determines the fibril core?': 'Aggrescan, FISH, FoldAmyloid, MetAmyl, and PASTA 2.0 predict a low propensity for amyloid formation across the FUS-LC.' ZipperDB, Zyggregator and WALTZ 'predict that certain short segments of FUS-LC may form amyloidlike structures' but 'with no consensus on the identities of these segments'. FIVE of these eight are in or adjacent to this project's own legacy set.

_WHY_THIS_ROW_IS_THE_CONTROL_PAIR_FOR_H4.the_computation: COMPUTED 16 Nov 2026 from P35637: FUS 39-95 is 3.5% proline-plus-charge (one proline, one charged residue in 57), and ALL 52 of its 6-residue windows sit at or below the worst deposited steric zipper (16.7%).
_WHY_THIS_ROW_IS_THE_CONTROL_PAIR_FOR_H4.why_that_matters: IT REMOVES THE COMPOSITIONAL EXCUSE ENTIRELY. For TRIOBP-1 324-348 one can argue a window-scanning predictor was not unreasonable to downweight a region that is 48% gatekeeper. FOR FUS 39-95 THAT DEFENCE IS UNAVAILABLE: there is nothing compositionally unusual about this region at all -- every single window is zipper-grade -- and five named predictors still failed to flag it.
_WHY_THIS_ROW_IS_THE_CONTROL_PAIR_FOR_H4.the_pairing: FUS 39-95 and tau PHF6 306-311 have essentially the SAME compositional profile (low gatekeeper, zipper-grade windows) and OPPOSITE prediction outcomes: tau is FOUND, FUS is MISSED. That is a far tighter control pair than tau versus TRIOBP-1, because it holds composition almost constant. H4 was promoted on the tau/TRIOBP-1 contrast; THIS PAIR IS THE BETTER TEST OF IT.
_WHY_THIS_ROW_IS_THE_CONTROL_PAIR_FOR_H4.the_three_row_structure: tau PHF6 16.7% gatekeeper, is a zipper, FOUND. FUS 39-95 3.5%, 52/52 windows zipper-grade, MISSED. TRIOBP-1 324-348 48.0%, 7/20 windows zipper-grade, MISSED. Composition does not order these outcomes -- which is Murray's own point, now doing work FOR the project rather than against it.
_WHY_THIS_ROW_IS_THE_CONTROL_PAIR_FOR_H4.honest_limit: n is still small and FUS is one protein. This strengthens H4; it does not by itself make a rate estimate. See PREREGISTRATION.md 7.

regions.frame: 320-RESIDUE FRAME = UniProt P09651-2 (isoform A1-A). READ THE NUMBERING NOTE BELOW BEFORE USING THIS ROW.
regions.evidence: The ordered fibril core determined by cryo-EM of fibrils grown from FULL-LENGTH protein. 'The fibril core is formed by 45 residues (Gly251 to Tyr295) from the LCD.' The remainder is disordered: 'Residues Met1 to Asp250 and Phe296 to Phe320 are not seen in our 3D map.'
regions.construct: FULL-LENGTH hnRNPA1, 'full-length hnRNPA1 protein (residues 1-320)'. THE CONSTRUCT COLUMN EARNS ITS KEEP HERE: the core is 45 of 320 residues with the other 275 present and disordered, so this is a core mapped IN CONTEXT rather than an isolated peptide that happened to aggregate. Compare FUS 39-95, which is 57 of 214 in the same situation.
regions.found_by: CRYO-EM STRUCTURE DETERMINATION. 'The reconstructed 3D map was used to build an atomic model of the fibril.' No predictor in the discovery path; the prediction tools were run afterwards and compared against the structure.
regions.source: Sharma et al. 2023, J Mol Biol -- Cryo-EM structure of the full-length hnRNPA1 amyloid fibril (PMC10530274)
regions.note: hnRNPA1 is on the psychiatric-aggregation candidate list already recorded in research_notes (the 2026 survey names it alongside DISC1, TRIOBP-1, CRMP1, dysbindin-1 and NPAS3), so this row widens the set without leaving the project's own protein universe.
regions.provenance_note: READ by the main session via PMC10530274 (open access), 16 Nov 2026. Publisher PDF not opened, so verified_against_publisher_pdf stays FALSE. The SEQUENCE, the 45-residue arithmetic and the cross-frame mapping are independently verified against UniProt.
regions.sequence_provenance: RETRIEVED FROM UniProt P09651-2 (320 aa), residues 251-295. Verified: the segment is 45 residues, begins with Gly and ends with Tyr, matching the paper's own 'Gly251 to Tyr295' and '45 residues' exactly -- two independent checks on the range.
regions.verified_against: Sharma et al. 2023, JMB -- PMC10530274 full text read by the main session.
regions.range_provenance: READ. 'The fibril core is formed by 45 residues (Gly251 to Tyr295) from the LCD.'
regions.circularity_basis: Core determined by cryo-EM; predictors run post hoc and compared against it, which is the permitted direction. The paper's conclusion is explicitly about the predictors failing, not about the predictors having chosen anything.
regions.stratum_basis: DOCUMENTED IN PRINT, WITH THE TOOLS NAMED, AND IT NAMES THE ENTIRE FROZEN LEGACY ARM. 'Five out of seven tested methods (Aggrescan, FoldAmyloid, Pasta 2.0, TANGO 2.2 and Amylpred 2)' -- these 'lacked any hit within the fibril cross-beta structure'. TANGO, AGGRESCAN and FoldAmyloid are the whole of PREREGISTRATION 5.1. The paper's summary judgement is that the tools 'do not specifically predict the sequence segments that form the fibril cross-beta structure'.
regions.THE_TWO_TOOLS_THAT_DID_HIT: STATE IT OURSELVES RATHER THAN BE SHOWN IT. 'Only two (ZipperDB and WALTZ) showed hits within these secondary structural elements.' WALTZ gave '4 true positives within the cross-beta structure'. For ZipperDB the paper disarms its own positive: 'the observation of true positives is compromised by a very high number (85) of false positives'. Neither tool is in the frozen legacy arm (5.1 = TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid, ProA), so the stratum is unaffected -- but note the PATTERN, which now has two instances: on DISC1 384-415 it was ANuPP that succeeded where the legacy arm failed, and here it is WALTZ. A SELECTIVE REPORT THAT MENTIONS ONLY THE FAILURES WOULD BE DISHONEST AND WOULD NOT SURVIVE REVIEW.
regions.NUMBERING_TRAP_RESOLVED_BY_LOOKUP_NOT_AR: data/regions.json's own _frame_traps_are_worse_than_assumed warns that hnRNPA1's two frames differ by an INTERNAL ALTERNATIVE EXON, so converting a range by a constant offset can yield a sequence that does not occur. HANDLED BY DIRECT SEQUENCE LOOKUP RATHER THAN BY ADDING A NUMBER. P09651-1 (isoform A1-B) is 372 aa; P09651-2 (isoform A1-A) is 320 aa; the paper uses the 320 frame. Searching the exact 45-mer in the 372-residue isoform locates it at 303-347. The constant offset of +52 HAPPENS TO BE CORRECT HERE, because this core lies C-terminal to the alternative exon -- but that was VERIFIED, not assumed, and it would NOT hold for any range spanning or upstream of the insert. ALWAYS QUOTE THIS ROW AS 251-295 IN THE 320 FRAME, and give 303-347 (372 frame) only with the isoform named.
regions.H4_ARCHITECTURE: COMPUTED 16 Nov 2026: 11.1% proline-plus-charge, and 34 of 40 6-residue windows sit at or below the worst deposited zipper (16.7%). LIKE FUS 39-95 AND UNLIKE TRIOBP-1 324-348, THIS IS A GATEKEEPER-POOR REGION THAT THE LEGACY ARM STILL MISSED -- a second instance where the compositional excuse is unavailable. It is also a LARKS/low-complexity Gly-Tyr-Asn core rather than a classic hydrophobic zipper, which is a candidate MECHANISM for the failure and is worth stating as a hypothesis, not a result.

_rows_deliberately_excluded.DISC1 L607F: DO NOT ADD. It appears in neither Cukkemane paper. The 2025 paper discusses L807-FS, a frameshift downstream of residue 807 -- a different residue and a different lesion. L607F's characterised phenotype is disrupted nuclear targeting and reduced ATF4 interaction, with no aggregation structure behind it.
_rows_deliberately_excluded.DISC1 S704C: Not an aggregation region. Measured from PDB 9RUX coordinates: its mouse equivalent is buried behind 96 heavy-atom neighbours with no cysteine sulfur within 11.76 A in any of four chains. A folding and packing variant.

_the_target_count: The plan sets a floor of roughly fifteen well-evidenced rows before proceeding. This file holds ten, of which several are sub-annotations or circular. Widening to every protein with fragment-level aggregation mapping -- not only the psychiatric ones -- is the outstanding task.
_the_inventory: A 146-row inventory across ~45 proteins now exists at research_notes/Mental illness aggregation structures/aggregation_region_ground_truth_inventory.md. About 20 rows are circular and about 40 are independent across ~25 proteins -- roughly five times this file. That answers the statistical-power problem. Rows must be read and verified before migrating them here.
_CPAD_CONTAMINATION_WARNING: DO NOT BULK-IMPORT FROM CPAD. The CANYA paper (Thompson 2025, Sci Adv, PMC12042874) states verbatim that "several of these methods (including TANGO, CamSol, and Aggrescan) were directly trained on sequences within CPAD", which violates out-of-sample evaluation on those datasets. Drawing rows from CPAD without per-row provenance checks reproduces exactly the violation that paper names. The same paper reports that on WALTZ-DB hexapeptides "no method significantly outperformed hydrophobicity".
_circularity_cannot_be_grepped: The predictor-provenance column cannot be filled by keyword search. Circularity is PROTEIN-specific, not lab- or journal-specific: the same laboratory in the same era produced rows of opposite status, and so did two segments of one protein. Four rows would be wrongly flagged by a grep, because a post-hoc remark about a predictor, or the use of a disorder or helix-propensity tool, is not prediction-guided discovery. Each row has to be read.
_frame_traps_are_worse_than_assumed: Beyond the TRIOBP-1 59-residue offset: hnRNPA1's two frames differ by an INTERNAL ALTERNATIVE EXON, so one commonly cited range exists only in the minor-isoform frame and converting it by a constant offset yields a sequence that does not occur. Tau's canonical accession is 758-residue big tau while the entire literature uses the 441-residue frame. Huntingtin's frame shifts with the repeat length.
_COAGGREGATION_IS_THREE_DIFFERENT_PHENOM: ADDED 15 Nov 2026. The word 'co-aggregation' names at least THREE unrelated things, and all three surface in searches this project runs. (1) PROTEIN hetero-aggregation -- two misfolded proteins forming mixed oligomers or fibrils. This is the only sense this project means. (2) EPIDEMIOLOGICAL / FAMILIAL co-aggregation -- diagnoses clustering in families. Liu F-C et al., Clin Epidemiol 10:631-641 (2018) is titled 'Familial aggregation of Parkinson's disease and COAGGREGATION WITH NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISEASES' and reports raised SCHIZOPHRENIA risk in first-degree relatives of PD patients. Any query pairing 'coaggregation' with 'schizophrenia' will return this literature, which is population genetics and says nothing about protein structure. See also Feldman et al., Eur J Epidemiol 29:49-56 (2014), 'modest familial co-aggregation between dementia and parkinsonism'. (3) BACTERIAL coaggregation -- specific adhesion between genetically distinct bacterial cells in biofilms, mediated by lectin-saccharide interactions. Nothing to do with amyloid. As of 15 Nov 2026 this repository is clean of senses (2) and (3); keep it that way, and label the sense whenever the word is used.

_SCHEMA_CIRCULARITY.added: 16 Nov 2026, by author decision: KEEP CIRCULAR ROWS, LABELLED, rather than dropping them. A benchmark that ships its contaminated rows with the contamination documented is more useful to other people than one that silently excludes them -- and the exclusions turned out to be the best-evidenced part of the work.
_SCHEMA_CIRCULARITY.circularity_status: CLEAN | CIRCULAR | UNDECIDABLE. CLEAN: the region was localised by truncation, deletion, substitution or an unbiased screen with NO aggregation predictor and no sequence/compositional heuristic in the DISCOVERY path. CIRCULAR: a predictor or sequence heuristic nominated the region and experiment then tested it. UNDECIDABLE: discovery path not recoverable from sources read.
_SCHEMA_CIRCULARITY.the_rule_that_makes_this_workable: PREDICTION USED AFTER MAPPING DOES NOT CONTAMINATE. A post-hoc predictor run on an already-mapped region is a mechanistic check, not a selection step. This is what keeps DISC1 384-415 clean despite Zaharija 2025 running five predictors on DISC1.
_SCHEMA_CIRCULARITY.circularity_is_TOOL_SPECIFIC: A region nominated by AmylPred2 is circular for AmylPred2 and for any consensus containing it, but a tool that did not exist at the time is being tested fairly on it. Circular rows may therefore serve as LABELLED POSITIVE CONTROLS for the modern arm -- with the selection bias stated, since a region legacy tools ranked top is predictable by construction and cannot test whether modern tools recover what legacy MISSED.
_SCHEMA_CIRCULARITY.how_these_rows_are_analysed: Separately, always, per CLAUDE.md. CIRCULAR rows are excluded from the primary statistic and reported as their own stratum. They are never silently pooled with CLEAN rows.

_SCHEMA_STRATUM.added: 16 Nov 2026, required by the PREREGISTRATION.md 7 amendment.
_SCHEMA_STRATUM.why: WIDENING THE SET MOSTLY ADDS TRUE POSITIVES, AND A TRUE POSITIVE CANNOT DISCRIMINATE MODERN FROM LEGACY PREDICTORS BECAUSE BOTH HIT IT. A region gets mapped cleanly and early precisely when it is a classic short hydrophobic or beta-prone motif -- which is what the predictors were built to detect -- so the literature is enriched for regions the predictors find. Power lives only where experiment and prediction DISAGREE.

values.DISCORDANT: Experiment and prediction disagree. THE PRIMARY STATISTIC IS COMPUTED ON THIS STRATUM ONLY.
values.CONCORDANT: The predictors find the region. Reported separately as a PIPELINE POSITIVE CONTROL -- it shows the predictors ran and scored sanely. Never pooled into the primary.
values.DISCORDANT_PROVISIONAL: Expected discordant from published results, not yet read out. Must resolve to DISCORDANT or CONCORDANT before the freeze.
values.PENDING: Assigned after the legacy arm runs and before the modern arm. That ordering is part of the freeze.

_SCHEMA_STRATUM.the_uncomfortable_count: AS OF 16 Nov 2026 THE DISCORDANT STRATUM HOLDS FOUR ROWS: TRIOBP-1 324-348, DISC1 384-415, FUS 39-95 and hnRNPA1 251-295. THREE OF THE FOUR WERE ASSIGNED FROM PUBLISHED POST-HOC PREDICTOR RUNS WITH THE TOOLS NAMED, requiring no run of ours. That is the sourcing lesson of the day: the binding constraint is DISCORDANT rows, not CLEAN rows, and the cheapest source of them is papers that ran predictors after mapping and published the failure. Searching for clean rows added three rows and zero test power; searching for published predictor failures added two discordant rows in one afternoon.

_ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1.finding: A POST-2010 PREDICTOR HAS ALREADY RECOVERED A REGION THE 2004-2010 GENERATION MISSED, ON ONE OF OUR TWO PSYCHIATRIC PROTEINS, PUBLISHED BY THE GROUP THAT MAPPED IT.
_ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1.what: Zaharija 2025 thesis section 4.3.5: of five predictors run on full-length DISC1, four gave hotspots 'dispersed throughout the entirety of the protein sequence' while ANuPP (2021) named AA 387-395 and AA 400-415 as highest nucleation capacity. Verified: both intervals lie entirely inside the mapped region 384-415.
_ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md's headline question is 'Do MODERN aggregation predictors recover the experimentally mapped regions of DISC1 and TRIOBP-1 that the 2004-2010 generation missed?' FOR DISC1, A PARTIAL ANSWER IS ALREADY IN PRINT, AND IT IS YES. This is not a pre-emption of PREREGISTRATION 5.2, which claims only that no PROTEIN LANGUAGE MODEL has been run on DISC1 or TRIOBP-1 -- ANuPP is not a PLM, and that claim survives. But the project can no longer present 'a newer tool finds what the old ones missed' as its own discovery for DISC1.
_ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1.what_the_project_must_do: CITE IT AS THE STARTING POINT AND POSITION AGAINST IT. The open questions it leaves are the ones worth asking: (1) does the PLM generation recover it, which nobody has tested; (2) does ANuPP's success GENERALISE to TRIOBP-1 324-348 and FUS 39-95, or was DISC1 a single lucky hit -- ANuPP has NOT been run on TRIOBP-1, and the thesis contains no TRIOBP-1 predictor runs at all; (3) ANuPP is a 2021 tool and sits in neither the frozen legacy arm nor the modern arm, which is now an obvious gap in the design.
_ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1.a_design_consequence_to_settle_before_th: ANuPP CURRENTLY HAS NO HOME IN THE PREREGISTRATION. PREREGISTRATION 5.1 freezes the legacy arm as TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid and ProA; 5.2 freezes the modern arm as AggreProt and AggrescanAI under a version-pinnable-and-local rule. A 2021 tool that has already succeeded on one of our rows belongs explicitly in one arm or in a named third category -- NOT left unmentioned, because it is the single strongest piece of evidence that the project's premise has a positive answer. The author should decide which, and it is a decision with a clear conflict of interest attached, since ANuPP succeeding is inconvenient for a project about predictor failure. SAY SO IN PRINT EITHER WAY.
_ANUPP_IS_PRIOR_ART_ON_H1.provenance: Thesis READ IN FULL 16 Nov 2026 (author-supplied). Frame equivalence and hotspot containment VERIFIED by the main session against UniProt Q9NRI5 and RefSeq NP_061132.2.

_A_PATTERN_THE_WRITE_UP_MUST_NOT_HIDE: IN EVERY DISCORDANT CASE WHERE A PAPER RAN SEVERAL TOOLS, AT LEAST ONE TOOL SUCCEEDED. On DISC1 384-415, four of five legacy-era tools missed the linker and ANuPP (2021) hit it precisely, naming 387-395 and 400-415. On hnRNPA1 251-295, five of seven missed the core while WALTZ scored four true positives inside it and ZipperDB hit it alongside 85 false positives. THE HONEST STATEMENT IS NOT 'THE PREDICTORS FAIL' BUT 'THE WIDELY USED 2004-2010 GENERATION FAILS WHILE SCATTERED OTHER TOOLS SOMETIMES SUCCEED, WITHOUT CONSENSUS' -- which is close to Murray 2017's own phrasing for FUS, that the hitting tools showed 'no consensus on the identities of these segments'. A write-up that reports only the failures would be selective and would not survive review. This also sharpens the real question: not whether prediction is impossible, but whether any tool succeeds RELIABLY ACROSS rows rather than sporadically on one.
